metadata.name: awk
metadata.displayName: awk - Text processing and data extraction
metadata.description: Pattern scanning and data processing language

installation.note: awk is a built-in command available on all Linux systems by default

overview.summary: awk is a powerful text processing and data extraction tool. It reads input line by line, splits into fields, and processes with patterns and actions. Excellent for extracting columns, processing structured data (CSV, logs), calculations, and report generation. More powerful than sed for complex text processing.

syntax.description: Process FILE(s) with PATTERN and ACTION. If no pattern, action applies to all lines. Fields are automatically split by whitespace.

options.use_case: Process CSV files or other delimited data
Set variables for use in awk script

breakdown.fields: awk automatically splits lines into fields by whitespace
breakdown.numbering: $1 = first field, $2 = second field, $0 = entire line

output_explanation.notes: Prints first field from each line. awk splits by whitespace automatically. $1 = first field, $2 = second, etc.

elements.meaning: Add third field to sum for each line

breakdown.accumulation: Accumulates sum as it processes each line

breakdown.end_block: END block runs after all input processed

output_explanation.notes: Sums values in third column. {sum+=$3} accumulates, END block prints final result. Very useful for data analysis.

breakdown.reorder: Can print fields in any order

output_explanation.notes: Prints columns in custom order. Comma adds space. Very useful for reorganizing data and creating reports.

misconceptions.title: awk is only for printing columns
misconceptions.reality: awk is a full programming language - can do calculations, conditionals, loops, functions, and much more. It's very powerful.
misconceptions.tip: awk is a programming language, not just a column extractor. Can do calculations, conditionals, loops, and complex processing.

misconceptions.title: awk only works with whitespace
misconceptions.reality: awk defaults to whitespace but can use any delimiter with -F flag. Essential for CSV, TSV, and other formats.
misconceptions.tip: Use awk -F',' for CSV, awk -F':' for colon-separated, etc. awk is very flexible with delimiters.

common_pitfalls.description: CSV processing fails because default separator is whitespace
common_pitfalls.solution: Always use awk -F',' for CSV files. Default separator is whitespace, not comma.
Remember: $1 = first field, $2 = second, $0 = entire line. Use awk '{print NF}' to see number of fields.

related_commands.relationship: Text processing; sed for simple edits, awk for complex processing
related_commands.description: Stream editor (simpler than awk for basic text editing)

related_commands.relationship: Column extraction; cut for simple columns, awk for complex
related_commands.description: Extract columns (simpler than awk but less powerful)

related_commands.relationship: Text search; grep finds, awk processes
related_commands.description: Search for patterns (awk can also search and process)

best_practices: Use $1, $2, etc. for fields, $0 for entire line
Use END block for final calculations and totals
Combine with other commands: ps aux | awk '{print $2}'
Use awk for complex processing, cut for simple column extraction
Test awk commands on sample data first
performance_tips: More efficient than multiple grep/sed commands for complex operations

additional_notes.field_separator: Default separator is whitespace. Use -F to specify delimiter (comma, colon, pipe, etc.)
additional_notes.field_numbering: $1 = first field, $2 = second, $NF = last field, $0 = entire line
additional_notes.programming: awk is a programming language - supports variables, conditionals, loops, functions, arrays
additional_notes.common_patterns: Very common: awk '{print $1}' (first column), awk -F',' '{print $2}' (CSV), awk '/pattern/ {print}' (filter), awk '{sum+=$3} END {print sum}' (calculate)
